core_problem: The lack of a systematic and standardized multi-dimensional benchmark to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) acting as agents across diverse, open-ended environments rather than traditional single-turn tasks.
methodology_summary: Introduction of AGENTBENCH, a multi-dimensional evaluation benchmark featuring 8 distinct environments with a Server-Client architecture. It supports modular, scalable, and API-centric evaluation with environment isolation and a unified toolkit to support multi-round interactive evaluation.
datasets_eval: AGENTBENCH (consisting of 8 distinct agent environments, including Bash and SQL testing)
empirical_results: Comprehensive benchmarking of 29 different LLMs, revealing a wide array of insights into agent performance and showcasing that current open-source LLMs commonly fail to solve problems in several highly challenging agent tasks.
explicit_limitations: Open-source LLMs frequently fail in complex environments; non-chat models require custom post-processors; and evaluated models are immediately deemed defeated if they fail to output legal actions within a specified number of rounds.
